subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and which write paths and defaults are in scope?
rationale: The request adds config surface and changes a security-sensitive filesystem boundary across core write paths, so automation should not choose the permanent policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
options.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state, schema/docs, and tests across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related write paths.

options.title: Use fixed per-path defaults
options.body: Avoid new config surface and continue fixing concrete writer defaults, such as readable media or workspace documents, where maintainers approve each boundary.

options.title: Document host-level setup only
options.body: Leave runtime permissions unchanged and document ACL, Docker user/group, umask, or NAS permission setup as the supported operator workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state, schema/docs, and tests across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related write paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail connects this person to the filesystem safety, tools.fs schema, and sandbox mutation boundaries involved in the product/security choice.
